subject: Chemistry
topic: Paramagnetism and the spin-only magnetic moment
title: A Balance That Counts Electrons: Paramagnetism and the Spin-only Magnetic Moment
summary: Every electron is a tiny magnet; in a pair the spins cancel, so only unpaired electrons make an ion paramagnetic. Count them from the ion's d configuration (singly up to d⁵, then pairing) and the spin-only formula gives the magnetic moment: μ = √(n(n+2)) BM, from 1.73 for one unpaired electron to 5.92 for Mn²⁺ (d⁵). A measured μ (Gouy balance) counts the unpaired electrons.

notes.title: 09 – Magnetic Properties: Paramagnetism and the Spin-only Magnetic Moment

keyPoints: **Paramagnetic** = attracted by a field (unpaired electrons); **diamagnetic** = weakly repelled (all paired).
Count **n**: write the ion's configuration (4s leaves first), fill the 3d orbitals **singly first**, then pair: d¹–d⁵ → n = d; d⁶–d¹⁰ → n = 10 − d.
μ peaks at **d⁵** (Mn²⁺ 5.92 calc., 5.96 observed); a measured μ tells you the number of unpaired electrons.

blocks.p: For 3d ions the orbital contribution is effectively quenched, so μ depends only on n. One unpaired electron: 1.73 BM.
Fe²⁺ and Co²⁺ read higher than spin-only because their orbital contribution is not fully quenched.
Z = 25, divalent ion in water: Mn²⁺ = 3d⁵, n = 5, μ = √(5 × 7) = √35 = **5.92 BM**.
